title: South Water and Lake fill out as 1835's row of stores
items: In 1835 the block fronts of South Water and Lake Streets, Wells to State, are now built up to about seven tenths of their length. 56 more reconstructed frame stores and boarding houses stand shoulder to shoulder at the street, the way Gifford drew the street round the first Tremont House.
Ten cottages that stood where the row now stands, or with their doors close behind it, moved to the backs of their own lots, households and all.
Every 1835 household now has a roof. The eight that were waiting are housed, and most of the new stores stand empty, ready for keepers the sources can name.
